input: Set up a weekly family game night

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The ages and number of family members directly determine which games are suitable and how the evening should be structured — a group with young kids needs very different games and pacing than a group of adults.
The day and time of the weekly slot determines scheduling feasibility and how much setup/wind-down time is realistic given school nights, work, bedtimes, etc.
Knowing whether this is starting from scratch (no games, no routine) or building on an existing collection and habit changes how much planning and purchasing is involved.
A budget for buying new games or supplies directly shapes what can be recommended or purchased; without it, suggestions may be impractical.
Game genre preferences (strategy, trivia, party, cooperative vs. competitive) ensure the night is tailored to what the family actually enjoys rather than generic picks.
Knowing where game night will be hosted and whether it will always be at the same location affects setup, storage of games, and whether guests outside the household are ever involved.
Understanding what 'successful' looks like — everyone participates willingly, it stays consistent for months, kids put down screens — defines what habits and structures need to be built in.

gold.taskTitle: Set up a weekly family game night
gold.taskDescription: Plan and establish a recurring weekly game night for the family, covering everything needed to make it a consistent and enjoyable routine.

questions.title: Who is joining — ages and number of family members?
questions.description: Identify the participants by age group and headcount to determine age-appropriate games and group dynamics.

questions.title: Which day and time works best each week?
questions.description: Pin down the recurring weekly slot that realistically fits everyone's schedules, including school nights and bedtimes.

questions.title: Do you already own games, or starting from scratch?
questions.description: Clarify whether there is an existing game collection to build on or if everything needs to be sourced fresh.

questions.title: What is your budget for buying new games or supplies?
questions.description: Establish a spending limit to keep game and accessory recommendations practical and affordable.

questions.title: What game styles does your family enjoy most?
questions.description: Understand genre preferences — strategy, trivia, party, cooperative, card games — to curate a fitting game lineup.

questions.title: Where will game night be hosted each week?
questions.description: Confirm the location (e.g., home dining table, living room) to plan for setup, seating, and game storage.

questions.title: What would make this feel like a lasting success to you?
questions.description: Define the outcome that matters most — consistent attendance, screen-free time, everyone engaged — to shape the right habits and structure.
